changeTriggers: tenant, identity, privilege or data-residency boundary change
new deployable, provider, worker, scheduler or paid infrastructure
irreversible migration, external API contract or release-provenance change

drivers.title: Fail closed at material human gates
drivers.statement: AI and automation may suggest or prepare, but authoritative sign-off, release, submission, deletion and provider effects require current server-enforced human authority and every applicable invariant.
acceptanceMeasures: No UI flag or stale preflight can bypass a material server gate
Authoritative responses are exposed only after durable commit

drivers.title: Tenant isolation and least privilege
drivers.statement: Every tenant-owned data path uses server-resolved organisation context, scoped authority and forced PostgreSQL RLS under a non-owner runtime identity.
acceptanceMeasures: Production startup rejects owner, superuser, BYPASSRLS or drifted privilege catalogues
Negative cross-tenant tests remain part of the database gate

scenarios.stimulus: An authenticated caller changes an organisation header or resource identifier to another tenant while concurrent legitimate tenant work is running.
scenarios.environment: Production-shaped PostgreSQL with FORCE RLS, the constrained runtime role and the normal tenant middleware stack.
scenarios.response: The server derives current authority, sets transaction-local tenant context and returns a non-disclosing denial without reading or mutating the other tenant.
scenarios.measure: 0 cross-tenant rows or object bytes disclosed; 0 cross-tenant mutations; 100% of negative isolation fixtures pass.
scenarios.releaseConsequence: Any cross-tenant disclosure or mutation is an immediate release blocker and rollback condition.

drivers.title: Evidence, provenance and auditability
drivers.statement: Material outputs and decisions retain versioned source bindings, deterministic digests, attributable audit events and independently verifiable release evidence.
acceptanceMeasures: Release and package identities are SHA-256 bound to exact inputs
Evidence gaps are labelled rather than inferred from a successful request

scenarios.stimulus: Retrieved tender content contains hostile instructions, lacks a current approved injection scan, contradicts its cited source or cannot support a factual claim.
scenarios.environment: Offline pre-ship corpus and any production-enabled AI retrieval/drafting path.
scenarios.response: The retrieval firewall blocks or abstains, preserves source provenance and prevents the result from becoming an authoritative fact or release input.
scenarios.measure: 100% injection containment on the approved hostile corpus; 0 contradicted or ungrounded claims released; every accepted claim has at least one exact approved source binding.
scenarios.releaseConsequence: Any injection escape or released ungrounded claim blocks model/prompt promotion and the affected product release.

drivers.title: Incremental modular monolith within current capacity
drivers.statement: Valo evolves the existing TypeScript, React, PostgreSQL and OpenAPI monorepo and adds deployables only when measured isolation, scale or ownership pressure justifies their operational cost.
acceptanceMeasures: Workspace dependency directions remain acyclic and allowlisted
A new deployable has a named owner, operational plan and ADR

drivers.title: Recoverable durable work
drivers.statement: Work that can outlive an HTTP request is admitted durably, leased and fenced, retry-bounded, idempotent and operator-recoverable before activation.
acceptanceMeasures: No activated durable effect depends on request lifetime or an in-memory queue
Crash, lease-fence, duplicate-effect and two-tenant tests pass before activation

scenarios.stimulus: Deadline-period arrivals reach twice the most recently observed 30-minute peak while object storage responds slowly or times out.
scenarios.environment: Production-shaped load rehearsal with bounded provider latency/failure injection and the durable worker boundary enabled only for the rehearsed capability.
scenarios.response: Accepted work receives one durable receipt, request threads do not claim a provider effect, leases recover after failure and users see a truthful queued or unavailable state.
scenarios.measure: 30-minute run at 2x observed peak; 100% accepted jobs durably recorded; 0 duplicate external effects; 0 false-success responses; p95 API latency remains within the approved release SLO.
scenarios.releaseConsequence: Do not activate the capability until the peak is calibrated and all binary safety measures pass; an SLO miss requires capacity or admission-policy review.

drivers.title: Provider neutrality with explicit activation
drivers.statement: Provider integrations sit behind typed boundaries and remain disconnected or disabled until configuration, privacy, residency, terms, health and fallback gates are approved.
acceptanceMeasures: Development, fake and disconnected adapters cannot claim production effects
Fallback never crosses an unapproved tenant policy or region

drivers.title: Versioned contracts and traceability
drivers.statement: External APIs, generated clients, rule packs, database migrations and architecture decisions are versioned and traceable to reviewed source evidence.
acceptanceMeasures: Generated client checks reject OpenAPI drift
Material architecture changes name their driver and ADR impact

drivers.title: Transactional concurrency correctness
drivers.statement: Material mutations use a declared lock order, current authority and state revalidation, compare-and-set transitions, idempotency and commit-before-response semantics.
acceptanceMeasures: Concurrent revocation or source mutation is serialized or rejected
A retry cannot bind one idempotency key to a different operation scope

scenarios.stimulus: A reviewer membership or report-sign-off grant is revoked, or an NDA is revoked, while sign-off or package export is in flight.
scenarios.environment: Production-shaped PostgreSQL integration test with the real advisory namespaces, row locks and request transaction lifecycle.
scenarios.response: The final transaction orders the revocation before or after the material action; stale authority/governance is rejected and no response capability is exposed before commit.
scenarios.measure: 0 sign-offs committed after an earlier effective authority revocation; 0 ZIP bytes exposed from stale NDA state; 100% race permutations end in one committed outcome or bounded 403/409 denial.
scenarios.releaseConsequence: Any stale-authority success, split durable state or stream-before-commit result blocks release.

scenarios.stimulus: A retention completion is requested for a project with an active legal hold, incomplete object reconciliation or a concurrently changing retention action.
scenarios.environment: Production-shaped retention workflow with tenant RLS, exact project locks and activation manifests.
scenarios.response: The workflow refuses destructive completion, preserves the hold and produces a bounded auditable blocker until reconciliation and certification are current.
scenarios.measure: 0 held records or objects deleted; 0 completion certificates before all mandatory actions are reconciled; 100% legal-hold negative fixtures pass.
scenarios.releaseConsequence: Any deletion under hold or premature certificate is a release blocker and privacy incident.

drivers.title: Privacy and data minimisation by boundary
drivers.statement: Logs, jobs, provider calls, release records and cross-tenant operations carry only the minimum identifiers and content needed for their declared purpose.
acceptanceMeasures: Operational signals contain no tenant, identity or tender-content dimensions
Provider activation records an approved data-governance boundary

scenarios.stimulus: An anonymous request uses a disallowed origin, oversized/non-JSON body, replayed key with changed content, automation trap, or attempts to submit tender documents; an authenticated upload is malformed or malware-flagged.
scenarios.environment: Public intake and governed upload paths under production configuration with scanners unavailable and available.
scenarios.response: Public intake accepts no document content and applies strict 16 KiB JSON, origin, idempotency and durable rate limits; governed files remain quarantined or rejected with no preview, extraction or release.
scenarios.measure: 100% hostile-intake fixtures rejected or quarantined; 0 unsafe bytes previewed/extracted/released; 0 public request bodies written to logs; changed-payload idempotency replay returns 409.
scenarios.releaseConsequence: Any unsafe-file release, origin bypass, PII body logging or changed-payload replay blocks release.

drivers.title: Verifiable release and recoverable operation
drivers.statement: A release binds exact merged source, artifacts, SBOM, target identity and deployment verification, with documented rollback, restore and incident procedures.
acceptanceMeasures: Deployment verification fails on source, manifest, URL, readiness or identity mismatch
Evidence distinguishes environment-declared identity from measured live bytes

scenarios.stimulus: The primary database/object-storage environment is unavailable or a release introduces suspected corruption.
scenarios.environment: Quarterly and pre-GA isolated restore rehearsal using an approved immutable backup and fixed recovery point.
scenarios.response: Operations restore into a new isolated target, re-attest identities/RLS, reconcile object manifests, audit/package hashes and provider side effects, then cut over only after smoke approval.
scenarios.measure: Measured RTO <= 4 hours; provisional RPO <= 24 hours until business-impact approval tightens it; 0 unreconciled duplicate provider effects; all restore acceptance checks pass.
scenarios.releaseConsequence: Missing restore evidence or a measured RTO/RPO miss blocks GA or requires a time-bounded, named risk acceptance.

drivers.title: Externally evidenced production dependencies
drivers.statement: Source configuration cannot by itself prove live provider approval, GitHub protection, platform schedules, alert delivery, backups or deployment state.
acceptanceMeasures: Status stays disconnected, not installed or externally unverified until a retained receipt exists
Repository checks never present desired platform policy as applied live state

drivers.title: Accessible and interruption-tolerant critical journeys
drivers.statement: Critical Valo journeys expose authority, status, errors and recovery in perceivable, operable and understandable forms across keyboard, screen reader, narrow viewport and low-bandwidth use.
acceptanceMeasures: No unrecovered critical accessibility violation in a release-critical task
Missing representative evidence is reported as missing, never inferred as a pass

scenarios.stimulus: A keyboard-only or screen-reader user is interrupted on a narrow, low-bandwidth connection while identifying a deadline blocker or completing a governed review action.
scenarios.environment: Pre-release critical-task walkthrough at desktop and narrow mobile viewport, including delayed responses and focus restoration.
scenarios.response: The interface preserves entered state where safe, announces status/errors, returns focus predictably, exposes the recorded deadline and next permitted action, and never represents cached/offline data as current authority.
scenarios.measure: 0 critical axe violations on automated public checks; 100% keyboard completion of the defined critical tasks; 0 keyboard traps; 0 unrecovered critical screen-reader or truthfulness defects.
scenarios.releaseConsequence: Any unrecovered critical accessibility or authority-truthfulness defect blocks release.
